endorsements.quote: Involve various stakeholders (end users and healthcare professionals) from diverse communities in the conceptualisation and development of the conversational AI tool
The stakeholders believed that any functionality, usability, and conversationality testing should involve patient groups and diverse communities in which health conversational AI is developed.
Ensure diversity in the design and implementation team throughout the project
Collaborating with health professionals can ensure the accuracy and relevance of medical content and the consideration of safety issues salient for specific social groups.
Before any training of conversational AI modules takes place, the conversational AI design teams can identify high-quality training datasets that incorporate diverse communities and populations.
Designers should implement emergency protocols to protect vulnerable users.
When implementing health conversational AI, it is crucial to determine accountability for safety breaches and unintended consequences.
Additionally, health chatbots should offer users an easy way to report safety concerns or file complaints.
Therefore, small-scale implementation activities must be first performed to address all issues related to integration.
Additionally, the deployment of a conversational AI requires careful consideration of medical device licensing and regulatory approvals during the initial stages of design and implementation.
Shared maintenance responsibilities between the supplier and the host, as well as issues of ownership, should be clarified.
If chatbots are to be implemented across various healthcare organisations, it may be necessary to initiate new pilot studies to ensure efficacy and user satisfaction.

It is important to conduct integration testing to ensure that conversational AI data exchange is continuous and accurate, particularly when conversational AI access electronic health records, appointment booking systems, prescription, and medication support systems where patient details are stored.
Ensure the continuation of patient care through the identification of alternative services

Monitoring the conversational AI features most frequently utilised by patients and incorporating a user feedback mechanism, such as a rating or suggestion system, can be invaluable for continuously enhancing the chatbot’s utility and effectiveness.
Regular and comprehensive testing of the conversational AI within the network of systems can also help identify potential issues before they result in significant disruptions.
Identify existing health disparities and explain how conversational AI can address them

Conversational AI designers should also conduct pilot studies with appropriate equity metrics to assess the type and level of behaviour change in the intended user group, aligned with defined health and behavioural outcomes.
Enable multiple language translation for culturally and linguistically diverse communities
Review and identify accessible patient-facing IT systems for wider reach in underserved communities
Ensure the ease of use for those with lower literacy or disability
Involve community champions and peer support groups in public and patient engagement activities

unlisted_practices: Provide a human contact pathway for further support and assistance in conversational AI tools.
Design conversational AI to recognise phrases indicating emotional crisis, self-harm or suicidal ideation and direct users to appropriate resources.
Involve native speakers in co-producing and translating conversational AI scripts rather than relying on automated translation.
Design conversational AI to communicate confidence thresholds and its limitations, and encourage users to seek professional medical advice for urgent conditions.
Publicly report safety incidents and adverse events involving conversational AI and the actions taken in response.
Provide comprehensive staff training on the chatbot's role in the clinical pathway and avoid increasing staff workload.
Give communities and patients advance notice (three months or more) before terminating a chatbot, with signposting to alternative services.
Coordinate updates to conversational AI so they do not disrupt interoperable systems, testing changes in a test environment first.
Use user-centred and culturally sensitive design, with neutral and medically accurate language, to reduce bias.
Assess the impact of AI termination on marginalised communities and healthcare service delivery.
Protect user privacy and secure data, including masking identifiers, encryption, and penetration testing for chatbots that collect sensitive information.
Conduct cost-effectiveness and sustainability assessments of conversational AI within healthcare settings.
Make conversational AI visible to diverse communities and provide information on its evidence base and ethical dimensions to build trust.

screen.reason: The paper uses qualitative stakeholder interviews and guideline analysis to develop a framework/roadmap (recommendations and guidelines) for equitable conversational AI design and implementation in healthcare rather than empirically testing an AI tool in practice.
